Some pointers from my years of Kung Fu and Boxing experience:

  • Always strike 3-5 times, your adrenaline will be surging in a real fight and you may very well miss with the first hit or two.

  • Always strike to break a limb, damage an internal organ or render the attacker unconscious. Never just throw a punch for the sake of it. Make each one count. This is where training and experience comes in.

  • A thrusting side kick to the side of the knee, if done correctly, will destroy the knee permanently, beyond the ability of surgical reconstruction.

  • A straight punch to the throat (either side of throat or adam's apple) will take down almost anyone, most of the time (nothing is guaranteed, always strike multiple times). Warning: Can be fatal.

  • A rising elbow (as if you are running your hand through the side of your hair like a 1950's greaser) if a great defence if someone is coming in swinging at you. They will most likely walk straight into your elbow coming up under their chin. Double up with both elbows to protect your head.

  • A straight punch to the sternum is also highly effective and can cause the attacker to drop their head in reflex (Follow up with knee or elbow under chin)

  • If your opponent is still standing after 3-5 hits or 5 seconds; Run! You will likely not be able to defeat them without taking damage yourself.

  • Never punch the head with a closed fist. Worst case: The teeth will cut your hand and the human mouth is extremely unhygienic. Best Case: You will hurt your hand reducing your fighting ability. Use the heel of your hand or your elbow instead.

  • Never attempt to engage a knife wielding attacker. EVER. Just Run. Even the most experienced masters will avoid a knife attacker, and only engage if they are literally cornered.

The above are just a brief overview. If you are feeling under treat where you live, seek out a traditional Chinese kung fu school with a respected master or another practical martial arts style (If they can trace their history back to the 5 families of the Shaolin temple it is usually a good sign). Avoid sports 'fighting' schools like the plague. There are no rules in a real fight and a sports style will hamper your ability to protect yourself.

What do you mean with "sports fighting schools"?

Any school that teaches 'point fighting' or the like (where you score points for a hit) and has a formalised system of match sparring. This is a hindrance in the real world as going for a 'point' is not a habit you want to pick up if you are interested in self defence, and you don't want to get into the mind set of there being 'rules' in a fight. There are no rules.

In my experience Kick Boxing and MMA etc are good for fitness, but self defence...not so much. To be fair though, obviously anything is better than nothing and good general fitness is a decent advantage in any fight; if you are stronger, quicker and have more stamina than the other guy.....well that's a nice advantage.

The main problem I have seen with sports fighters is they go in with stupid, flashy looking kicks, constantly. A decent trained 'real world' fighter will punish that very severely, like 'broken leg' severely! A real 'life in the balance' fight doesn't look pretty or 'flash'. It looks quick and brutal.

You want to be looking for somewhere that teaches targeted blows, blocking, body conditioning, one step sparring and power generation through correct body movement. Those are all good signs. A traditional Kung Fu or Judo school would be a good start; Lau Gar, Hung Gar, Seven Star Mantis are all good 'real world' styles. I have also heard good things about Krav Maga from people I respect, but have not tried it myself.

I've taught martial arts before, and here are my tips for your particular situation:

  • GET IN SHAPE. Size, strength, and stamina matters in any self-defense situation. Being strong will automatically increase your abilities to fight, regardless of knowledge.

  • Carry around a sturdy handbag, or purse. Keep your phone, and important things inside your pockets, and have a purse with relatively heavy objects inside that won't be considered a weapon. Then if you're attacked, kick your attacker away with your foot, or push them off, and use your purse like a flail. Whack them on the side of the head, or if you want just hold the entire purse, and use it to smash their nose in.

  • A handful of small denomination coins. Just keep them in your pocket. If someone attacks you, throw all of these coins, as hard as you can at their face, and flee.

  • An umbrella is still a good weapon. Just use it like a regular, old stick. Your umbrella will break but it will hurt them. Smash them up, until your rain protector is in two pieces.

  • There are simple, weaponless attacks you can do too. Target for example the groin, eyes, and the ears. Front kick to the groin, thrust your fingers into the eyes, or with a cupped hand strike over the ear. Of course once you do these, and you see they're stunned, run away. It's not magic. It's a surprise attack, a one-use move. Your main objective in all situations is to escape.

  • Verbalize. Tell them in a loud assertive voice that you don't want trouble, and that they should leave you alone. Legally this will help you because if there are witnesses they will frame you as the victim, who didn't want to be harmed.

  • Most importantly, You should take some martial arts classes. These things I listed are okay, but to be able to defend yourself properly you need training. **Daily Devotional**

**April 10**

*6 And again, when he bringeth in the firstbegotten into the world, he saith, And let all the angels of God worship him. (Hebrews 1:6 KJV)*

Some religious organizations like the Jehovah’s Witnesses say that Jesus was not God, but just an Angel. The Bible says that Angels are only to worship Jehovah God (Nehemiah 9:6), so this shows that Jesus was God, not just an Angel. God said that the Angels were to worship Jesus at His birth (Luke 2:13). The Bible tells us that Jesus was the Creator of the Angels themselves (Ephesians 3:9), so they sure would worship their Creator.

The fact that Jesus was God in the flesh while here on earth is not only recorded in the New Testament, but in some prophecies of the Old Testament (Psalms 110:1). So the Divinity of Jesus should not be questioned, and salvation is not possible unless you believe that Jesus is the Son of God (John 20:31), and died for your sins, and rose again to be seated at the right hand of God the Father in Heaven (Romans 10:9-10). No Christian can believe otherwise, and keep his salvation. Thank you Lord for giving us your Word and explaining so much, that we might know you and the Father in an intimate way (John 17:3).

Devotional by Pastor Joe W. Green, www.Infinite-Faith.com
